title: Git push get an AI API: Ryan Fox-Tyler
talk_summary: This is a live workshop demo of HyperMode, a commercial platform for deploying AI functions (AssemblyScript compiled to WASM) with auto-generated GraphQL endpoints, hosted models, and in-memory vector collections. The concrete patterns shown are basic RAG over GitHub issues: fetch data via REST, prompt an LLM to summarize trends, and use a small HuggingFace classifier plus an embedding model for similar-issue search.

takeaways.technique: Purpose-built small classifier instead of a large LLM for triage labels
takeaways.what_they_do: They use a small HuggingFace model (BERT MNLI fine-tuned on GitHub issues) to classify issue type (bug/feature/question) rather than calling GPT, and note it is auto-provisioned as a dedicated instance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's pre-trained on giab issues so it's a purpose built model we don't need to spend time model training here ... this is a really small model

takeaways.technique: Confidence threshold as plain code on classifier output
takeaways.what_they_do: They suggest reading the model's confidence score and writing a threshold comparison in code to decide whether to trust a label, rather than training a new model.

takeaways.technique: Hybrid model + deterministic validation to catch model errors
takeaways.what_they_do: When the LLM accepted 'P doctor' as a valid P-occupation, they added a dictionary check alongside the model so traditional code filters model output.

takeaways.technique: Embedding-function-bound vector collection for similar-item search
takeaways.what_they_do: They define a collection plus an embedder function so every insert (code or CSV upload) is auto-embedded with the same model used at query time, then do top-3 similarity search returning text.
Every model call is logged with input, output, latency, and token count in an inference history view, plus per-function raw logs, to debug chained model calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're going to get one of these entries to understand how long it took what was the input what was the output
